[U2, U3, route guard] merge-authority's route() builds the v2_branch_without_plan refusal per registered active plan: the policy branch_pattern with <plan_id> filled by re.escape(plan_id) and <goal_id> left generic, compiled with re.IGNORECASE; neither a registered plan's pattern nor the live policy's branch_pattern is ever applied with a generic <plan_id>. [O10, route] A completed v1 entry's retire record is a top-level retired_v1[] key of .ai/workflows/northstar-readiness-v2.json, never an entry of plans[]. route() skips registry entries whose status is not active, so a retired or superseded plan never blocks a --pr call; an active entry that fails to load still refuses (plan_unloadable, fail closed, the certificate test's unmodified case at :491). tests/readiness_v2_certificate_test.py proves that a goal PR still routes to v2 and a docs/ PR to v1 after the retired_v1 record lands.

[O4, reserved namespace] modules/merge-authority.md and modules/readiness-v2.md document the reserved branch namespace: for each registered active plan, its policy branch_pattern with that plan_id and any goal id, case-insensitive. An active goal is a goal of an active registry entry whose goal-branch PR merge commit is not yet an ancestor of origin/<target> (reusing the observer's dependency-ancestry facts); the reserved set is the union of what is active at the PR's base commit and at the current origin/<target>. Once v2 is live on origin/<target>, a non-goal PR takes the v1 verdict lane only if its diff touches no reserved path, unless the replay exception or the sidecar-tighten lane below covers the touch: the policy file .ai/policies/readiness-policy.json, the v2 registry .ai/workflows/northstar-readiness-v2.json, .ai/handoff/readiness-v2/** and every active goal's other scope paths (a path equal to or under a scope entry). Any other touch refuses with v2_scope_outside_goal (exit 4). The planning-publication paths are exactly the v2 registry .ai/workflows/northstar-readiness-v2.json and .ai/handoff/readiness-v2/** (reserved; a non-goal PR touches them only through an exception), plus the free planning-input paths .ai/traceability/graph.json, plan-scoped spec copies under docs/specifications/ACTIVE/ and the request documents .ai/handoff/<plan_id>-plan-approval-request.json and .ai/handoff/<plan_id>-plan-approval.md; they and .ai/ci/local-ci.json are never reserved through goal scope. The policy file is never covered by any exception and merges only through a policy goal's v2 certificate. For v2 merges the merge-certificate/1 is the host-policy audit record (O4).

[O4, replay exception] A non-goal PR whose reserved-path changes are exactly a publish-v2 replay takes the v1 lane. The observer replays the publication with the pinned origin/<target> publish-v2 driver (verified by readiness-dependency-v2.json, never the PR's own code) in a scratch checkout whose reserved paths are reset to the PR base, with the PR head's new goals.json, sidecar.json and optional policy-candidate.json as inputs, and byte-compares only the reserved-path part of the diff (the registry and .ai/handoff/readiness-v2/**); every other path, including the spec copy, the request documents and the traceability graph, is free and not compared. The diff may add a new plan id. It may replace an existing registry entry only when that plan has no merged and no open goal PR (which still permits the planned P5 republish), and every such replacement is reported under the notice code v2_plan_entry_replaced. A byte mismatch, or a replacement of a plan with a merged or open goal PR, is not covered and refuses with v2_scope_outside_goal.

[O1, sidecar tighten lane] A non-goal PR whose diff is limited to the sidecar.json of existing generations takes the v1 lane when each changed sidecar's base-to-head change passes the merged tighten-only check (validate_sidecar and sidecar_leq, O1); any loosening refuses with v2_sidecar_not_tightening.

[U2, diff observation and head binding] The changed paths are observed as the merge-base (three-dot) diff between the PR's observed base and head, or as the hosted changed-files list with previous_filename checked on renames, so a file renamed into a reserved path touches it. Pagination or truncation (GitHub caps the files list at 3000) fails closed, and an unobservable file list refuses outside tests; only the in-process test stub may default to an empty list. A v1-lane decision prints the observed PR head (a merge-decision/1 with decision v1 and that head) before the unchanged v1 adapter runs, and modules/merge-authority.md requires the v1-lane merge to use gh pr merge --match-head-commit at that head.

[Routing tests] tests/readiness_v2_certificate_test.py appends cases: a planning PR adding a generation, with a spec copy and request documents, takes v1; a maintenance PR after the plan completes takes v1; a docs/x PR touching the policy file is refused; a PR touching an active goal's scope is refused with v2_scope_outside_goal; a replay that replaces an active plan with goal PRs is refused; a sidecar hold added takes v1; a loosened sidecar is refused with v2_sidecar_not_tightening; a truncated file list is refused; a file renamed into a reserved path is refused.

Gaps are classified by kind, not by gate stage: the approval family (approval_* codes, plan_approval_missing, ownership_unresolved) counts as the one approval gap; the deferred kinds are exactly branch_target_mismatch, pr_required, hosted-check gaps (check_* and protection_check_unsatisfied), review_lane_missing, threads_unobserved and dependency_incomplete, listed in the report as deferred, never hidden and never counted as passed; every other gap blocks publication, including tooling, fixture, B5 ancestry and harness_trust. A v2 publication carries no holds; a v1 bundle takes the unchanged v1 path (AC-3). Tested in tests/northstar_v2_publish_test.py.

Approval capability derives from the policy's accept list: an approver principal (ai-catapult-plan-approval) counts when ssh-tag is accepted, an agent-approval principal (ai-catapult-agent-approval) counts only when agent-self is accepted, and an in-session form needs no approval principal.
